canonical_claim: GE Aerospace is a two-segment aerospace company whose commercial business is predominantly aftermarket and whose products are certificated by aviation regulators.
recommended_action: Keep the revenue-mix and product-life facts adjacent to the segment descriptions. Without them a reader takes CES for an engine manufacturer and misreads every margin figure downstream.
synthesis: These units describe what the company is, and they are complementary rather than convergent -- each states a different fact and none is evidence for another. Two structural facts carry most of the weight: Commercial Engines & Services is roughly 73% of revenue with services at 75% of that segment, so this is an installed-base business rather than a manufacturing one; and engines operate for decades after sale, which is what makes a platform selection compound across a service life. The regulatory units are not background: type certificates, production certificates and repair station certificates are the conditions under which the business may operate at all.

canonical_claim: GE reports supply disruption and tariff cost as conditions it is operating under, not as contingencies, and is investing against both.
recommended_action: Keep the indicative framing. Merging these into the risk factors would convert something the company says is happening into something it says might.
synthesis: Four units stating the operating environment in the indicative rather than the conditional: material availability and supplier delivery have impacted production, and tariffs will result in additional cost. That grammatical difference from the risk factors is the point -- these are reported facts, not disclosed possibilities. The $1 billion in US manufacturing, 5,000 hires and $1 billion of MRO capacity are the stated response. The January 2026 segment reorganization is a subsequent event that will break comparability with the figures in this filing.

canonical_claim: GE Aerospace grew 2025 revenue 18% to $45.9 billion with net income from continuing operations of $8.6 billion, driven by commercial services volume and pricing, against a backlog of $190.6 billion.
recommended_action: Keep the figures with their stated drivers and keep the Corporate & Other gain visible. A three-year revenue series without it invites the wrong inference about 2023.
synthesis: The year's results and their stated drivers, agreeing because they are one set of accounts rather than independent measurements. Three things a reader needs and could lose: services RPO of $163.0 billion is roughly six times equipment RPO, so the backlog is a service annuity rather than an order book; 2023 net income exceeded 2024's because of a $5.8 billion gain in Corporate & Other, not because operations were better; and CES profit growth was partially offset by higher install engine volume, which is the structural feature that selling engines dilutes margin while servicing them creates it.

canonical_claim: GE's effective tax rate of 14.1% sits well below the US statutory rate because of lower-taxed non-US earnings, and its discontinued operations carry retained exposures from businesses it no longer runs.
recommended_action: Keep the rate, the reason and the cash figure together. A rate without its jurisdictional explanation cannot be forecast.
synthesis: The tax units explain a rate rather than merely reporting it, which is what makes them usable: the reason is a mix of jurisdictions, bounded by the US minimum tax on foreign earnings. Cash taxes paid of $585 million against a $1,405 million provision is a gap worth carrying separately. The discontinued-operations units are the same shape as the legal and insurance material -- obligations that outlived the businesses that created them, with Bank BPH litigation still open.

canonical_claim: GE targets strong investment grade ratings, holds $20.5 billion of borrowings against a $15.0 billion buyback authorization, and reports that its debt contains no material credit rating covenants.
recommended_action: Keep the covenant absence and the restricted cash. Both are qualifications on figures that read as unconditional without them.
synthesis: The capital structure and the policy governing it. The most useful unit is a stated absence: substantially all debt agreements contain no material credit rating covenants, which means a downgrade would raise cost without triggering acceleration. Read against the refinancing risk factor, the two together bound what a downgrade would actually do. The $0.4 billion of cash under currency control restrictions is a specific qualification on otherwise-reported liquidity.

canonical_claim: GE's run-off long-term care insurance book holds 201,700 policies with $23.8 billion of GAAP reserves whose value turns on morbidity, mortality and premium-increase assumptions the filing quantifies.
recommended_action: Keep every sensitivity with its shock and its dollar figure. Stripped of the numbers this becomes an assurance rather than a disclosure, and the numbers are the disclosure.
synthesis: The most quantitatively usable material in the filing, and the only place it states what a change in assumption is worth in dollars. The sensitivities are the payload: a 5% increase in incidence rates is $600 million adverse; a 5% reduction in disabled life deaths or a 5% increase in utilization, $1,200 million each. Note that reduced mortality is adverse here -- policyholders living longer costs money -- which inverts the intuition a reader brings from a life book. The policy characteristics explain why the tail is long: 63% have lifetime benefit periods and 77% inflation protection.

canonical_claim: GE organizes its risks into strategic, operational, financial and legal categories, and several are concentrations that follow directly from the business it describes.
recommended_action: Keep the four risks that carry a mechanism or an admission. Do not present the category definitions as findings -- they are an organizing scheme.
synthesis: Risk factors are written to be comprehensive rather than discriminating, and several here resolve to the same shape -- something adverse may occur and may have a material adverse effect. What survives that as usable: the commercial aviation concentration is a restatement of the 73% revenue fact from a different section; the product safety risk carries an admission that costs have already been incurred; the supply chain risk names supplier qualification time as the reason substitution is slow, which is specific to a certificated industry; and the spin-off risk names a concrete possibility, that a completed tax-free separation is later determined taxable.

canonical_claim: Management concluded internal control over financial reporting was effective, and the auditor identified two critical audit matters, both estimate-driven.
recommended_action: Keep the critical audit matters linked to the policy and insurance entries they concern. Read alone they are procedural; read together with the estimates they name, they are a map of the filing's soft spots.
synthesis: The control assertion and the auditor's own account of where the accounting is hardest. The two critical audit matters -- revenue recognition on long-term service agreements, and future policy benefits -- correspond exactly to the two areas the filing itself discloses the most estimation sensitivity about, which is an independent corroboration of where the risk sits rather than a coincidence. Deloitte has served since 2020.

canonical_claim: GE's accounting policies define how its largest revenue stream, its investments and its fair values are measured, and several are stated as conditions rather than descriptions.
recommended_action: Carry the policies in applicable form. A reader who cannot tell that service revenue is an estimate against forecast cost cannot interpret the segment margin.
synthesis: The definition-shaped part of the filing, and the part a reader most needs stated rather than summarized. Percentage-of-completion on long-term service agreements is the policy behind the largest revenue line and the first critical audit matter: revenue is recognized against an estimate of total costs, so the estimate is the revenue. CFM International is named as the most significant equity-method related party, which places a material part of the commercial business outside the consolidated statements. The fair value units state which instruments are valued by quoted price and which by internal model.

canonical_claim: GE carries a $5.4 billion pension deficit across plans with $28.5 billion of obligations, including a $2.9 billion unfunded supplementary plan.
recommended_action: Keep the deficit, the unfunded portion and the participant counts. A deficit figure without the funded/unfunded split understates what is actually owed with nothing behind it.
synthesis: Absent from the results discussion entirely and recovered only by the repair round. The deficit is roughly an eighth of annual revenue. Two features make it structural rather than operational: the supplementary plan is unfunded with no assets against a $2.9 billion obligation, and the covered retiree population is larger than the active workforce of 57,000. Expected 2026 payments of approximately $220 million are the near-term cash consequence, which is small relative to the obligation.

canonical_claim: GE retains legal, environmental and indemnification exposures from businesses it has separated or exited, several quantified and several still open.
recommended_action: Keep the dates and the amounts. 'Various litigation in the normal course' is the sentence these units exist to replace.
synthesis: The obligations that outlived the businesses. Shareholder derivative suits have been running since 2018 and the Mahar class action since July 2018 -- neither appears anywhere in the results discussion. Environmental remediation and worker exposure claims run at roughly $190 million a year, a recurring cash cost. Indemnities to GE HealthCare under the tax matters agreement are stated as fully reserved. The product warranty balance of $595 million is the financial expression of the product quality risk the risk factors describe in words.

canonical_claim: GE reports free cash flow of $7.7 billion on a defined non-GAAP basis, earns most revenue outside the US, and does not report assets by segment.
recommended_action: Keep the reconciliation and the segment-asset absence. Both are the difference between a figure a reader can check and one they must accept.
synthesis: Three things the front of the filing implies and only these units establish. Non-US revenue of $27.7 billion exceeds US revenue of $18.2 billion, with Asia nearly doubling since 2023 -- which is what makes the tariff and trade-control discussion material rather than formal. The free cash flow reconciliation shows the measure adds back separation and restructuring cash actually spent, so it is a defined measure rather than a claim. And GE states it does not report segment assets because its CODM does not use them, meaning segment return on capital cannot be computed from this filing at all.

canonical_claim: GE discloses a cybersecurity framework with named processes and board-level Audit Committee oversight, and states it has experienced and expects to continue experiencing cyberattacks.
recommended_action: Keep the admission distinct from the framework. The framework describes intent; the admission reports fact.
synthesis: A compliance disclosure that reads as one. The processes are specific enough to check -- incident response plan and testing, role-based training, third-party supplier risk assessment, external posture assessment -- and the governance names both the Audit Committee and the CIO. The unit that carries information rather than assurance is the admission that attacks have already occurred and are expected to continue, stated in the past and future indicative rather than conditionally.

canonical_claim: GE's forward-looking statements are qualified by an enumerated list of uncertainties and an explicit refusal to update them.
recommended_action: Keep the no-update statement. It is the condition under which every projection in the corpus should be read.
synthesis: Boilerplate in form, but two things in it are load-bearing. The refusal to update means every forward-looking figure in the filing is fixed as of the filing date and will not be corrected. And the enumerated uncertainties are more specific than the risk factors in places -- naming tariffs, defense budgets, emissions trading regimes and third-party cybersecurity breaches. The governance units identify who signed and the independence of the Audit Committee.
